concepts.name: Aeolian Erosion Processes: Deflation, Abrasion, and Attrition
key_dimensions: Distinction between deflation (removal of loose material) vs. abrasion (sandblasting of rock surfaces) — UPSC frequently conflates these
Role of attrition in rounding and reducing sand grain size during transport
Conditions that favour each process: grain size, wind velocity thresholds, vegetation cover
Comparison with fluvial/glacial erosion to highlight uniqueness of aeolian action

concepts.name: Modes of Aeolian Sediment Transport: Saltation, Creep, and Suspension
key_dimensions: Mechanics of each mode — saltation as dominant mode (~75–80% of sand movement), surface creep driven by saltation impact, suspension for fine dust
Grain size thresholds governing which mode operates (clay/silt in suspension; sand in saltation/creep)
Hjulström-curve analogy for wind: why very fine particles require higher velocity to entrain than medium sand
Geomorphic significance: suspension links aeolian to loess deposition far beyond desert margins

concepts.name: Deflation Hollows (Blowouts) and Desert Depressions
key_dimensions: Formation mechanism: sustained deflation of unconsolidated sediment lowering the surface
Relationship to water table — deflation halts when moisture binds sediment or water table is reached (oasis formation)
Scale variation: small blowouts on coastal dunes vs. large structural depressions (e.g., Qattara Depression, Egypt)
UPSC trap: distinguishing tectonic/structural desert basins from purely deflation-formed depressions

concepts.name: Desert Pavement (Reg/Serir/Gibber): Formation and Significance
key_dimensions: Formation by deflation removing fine particles, leaving a lag of coarse pebbles/stones — armour effect halts further deflation
Regional terminology: Reg (North Africa/Arabia), Serir (Libya), Gibber (Australia) — UPSC asks for regional names
Role of wetting-drying cycles and salt weathering in upward migration of clasts (desert mosaic hypothesis)
Significance as indicator of past aeolian activity and surface stability; contrast with sand seas (ergs)

concepts.name: Ventifacts and Dreikanter: Wind-abraded Rock Features
key_dimensions: Formation: abrasion by saltating sand on stationary rocks producing faceted, polished surfaces
Dreikanter — three-faced ventifact; indicates prevailing wind direction changes or rock rotation
Pitting, grooving, and polishing as sequential stages of abrasion intensity
Palaeoclimatic significance: ventifacts found outside present deserts indicate past arid conditions (e.g., Thar margins)

concepts.name: Yardangs: Streamlined Wind-Erosion Ridges
key_dimensions: Formation: differential abrasion of soft and hard rock layers aligned parallel to dominant wind, creating elongated ridges and furrows
Morphology — whale-back or inverted boat shape; steeper windward face, tapered leeward end
Mega-yardangs vs. small yardangs: scale and lithological controls
UPSC trap: distinguishing yardangs (erosional) from longitudinal dunes (depositional) — both are wind-parallel elongated features

concepts.name: Inselbergs, Bornhardts, and Pediplains: Erosional Residuals in Arid Landscapes
key_dimensions: Inselberg as isolated hill rising abruptly from a flat pediplain — formed by differential weathering and pediplanation
Bornhardt: dome-shaped inselberg in massive, jointed-free crystalline rock (exfoliation-dominated); distinction from castle koppie (joint-controlled)
Role of aeolian abrasion at base vs. deep chemical weathering beneath surface in two-stage formation
UPSC overlap: inselbergs in semi-arid savanna (e.g., Deccan) vs. hyper-arid deserts — not exclusively aeolian but linked to arid geomorphology syllabus

concepts.name: Sand Dune Morphology and Classification: Transverse, Longitudinal, Star, Barchan, Parabolic
key_dimensions: Wind regime and sand supply matrix: transverse dunes (unidirectional wind, abundant sand); longitudinal/seif (bidirectional or strong unidirectional, limited sand); star dunes (multidirectional wind)
Barchan dune — crescent shape, horns point downwind, forms with limited sand and unidirectional wind; migration rate inversely proportional to size
Parabolic dune — U-shape with horns pointing upwind (anchored by vegetation); common in semi-arid/coastal settings — UPSC trap: opposite orientation to barchan
Slip face angle (~34°, angle of repose of dry sand) and its geomorphic significance for avalanching and dune migration

concepts.name: Barchan Dunes: Dynamics, Migration, and Significance
key_dimensions: Precise conditions: unidirectional wind, scarce sand, hard flat surface — distinguishes from other crescent dunes
Internal structure: windward gentle slope vs. steep leeward slip face; grain-size sorting (coarser at base, finer at crest)
Migration rates (can be metres per year) and hazard to infrastructure (roads, oases, pipelines) — policy/application angle
UPSC trap: barchanoid ridges (coalescing barchans with abundant sand) vs. true isolated barchans

concepts.name: Seif (Longitudinal) Dunes: Formation Debate and Characteristics
key_dimensions: Two competing theories: Bagnold's helical vortex theory vs. bimodal wind resultant theory — UPSC may ask which is more accepted
Characteristic parallel ridges extending for kilometres; found in Sahara, Arabian Desert, Simpson Desert (Australia)
Distinction from transverse dunes: orientation relative to wind (parallel vs. perpendicular)
Sand supply and wind consistency as key controls; comparison with coastal foredunes

concepts.name: Star Dunes (Pyramidal Dunes): Multidirectional Wind Indicators
key_dimensions: Formation under variable/multidirectional wind regimes — arms radiate in multiple directions
Among the tallest dunes (e.g., up to 300 m in Sahara/Rub' al Khali); relatively stationary compared to barchans
Palaeoclimatic use: star dune preservation indicates past variable wind conditions
UPSC trap: star dunes as net sand sinks — sand converges rather than migrates linearly

concepts.name: Loess: Aeolian Silt Deposits — Formation, Distribution, and Significance
key_dimensions: Origin: wind-transported silt (0.01–0.05 mm) deposited beyond desert/glacial margins; China's Loess Plateau as world's largest deposit
Unstratified, porous, vertically jointed structure — leads to distinctive loess landforms (loess terraces, gullies)
Pedogenic significance: highly fertile loess soils (e.g., North China Plain, Great Plains USA, Ukraine); agricultural productivity link
UPSC angle: loess in India (Punjab-Haryana alluvial plains debated), loess as proxy for past glacial-aeolian coupling, hydrogeological importance (aquifer potential)

concepts.name: Erg, Reg, and Hamada: Desert Surface Types and Their Spatial Distribution
key_dimensions: Erg (sand sea): vast areas of sand dunes — covers only ~20–25% of deserts (UPSC favourite trap: 'deserts are mostly sand' is a misconception)
Reg/Serir: stone pavement surface — most extensive desert surface type
Hamada: bare, rocky plateau surface swept clean of sand; flat or gently undulating
Distribution in Sahara as classic example; India's Thar analogues (sandy erg in Rajasthan vs. rocky outcrops)

concepts.name: Desert Varnish (Rock Varnish): Formation and Palaeoclimatic Significance
key_dimensions: Composition: thin coating of manganese oxides, iron oxides, and clay on rock surfaces — not purely aeolian but aeolian dust is the Mn/Fe source
Formation mechanism: microbial concentration of Mn from aeolian dust in alternating wet-dry cycles
Use in rock art preservation and relative dating of desert surfaces
UPSC angle: distinguishing desert varnish (surface coating) from caliche/duricrust (subsurface pedogenic feature) — common confusion in answers

concepts.name: Pediment and Pediplain: Arid Erosion Surfaces
key_dimensions: Pediment: gently sloping bedrock surface at mountain base, thinly veneered with alluvium — formed by lateral planation and sheet wash
Pediplain: coalescence of pediments from multiple directions creating a vast flat plain with residual inselbergs
W.M. Davis cycle of arid erosion vs. L.C. King's pediplanation theory — UPSC differentiates these two models
Aeolian reworking of pediment surface materials linking to deflation and desert pavement formation

concepts.name: Sand Dune Stabilisation, Desertification, and Human Dimension
key_dimensions: Natural stabilisation: vegetation colonisation binding sand, moisture increase, chemical cementation
Anthropogenic destabilisation: overgrazing, deforestation triggering reactivation of fossil dunes (e.g., Rajasthan, Sahel)
Sand dune movement as a desertification indicator — UNCCD framework and India's action plan link
Mitigation measures: shelter belts, sand fences, grass planting — Great Green Wall of Africa as policy example

concepts.name: Playas (Takyr/Salina/Kavir): Ephemeral Desert Lakes and Salt Flats
key_dimensions: Formation: episodic water accumulation in enclosed desert basins evaporating to leave salt/clay flats
Regional nomenclature: Playa (USA), Kavir (Iran), Takyr (Central Asia), Salina (general) — UPSC asks for correct regional terms
Evaporite mineral sequence (carbonates → sulphates → halides) and economic significance (potash, borax, lithium brines)
Aeolian link: deflation of dried playa surface generates dust storms and loess; playas as source of aeolian sediment

concepts.name: Dust Storms and Haboobs: Meteorological-Geomorphic Interface
key_dimensions: Haboob: intense, convection-driven dust wall (Sudan, Arabian Peninsula, Arizona) — distinguished from synoptic-scale dust storms by origin mechanism
Dust transport pathways: Saharan dust to Amazon (fertilisation), Arabian dust to Indian Ocean (iron fertilisation of phytoplankton)
Geomorphic role: dust storms as primary agents of deflation and loess transport
UPSC current affairs angle: dust storm frequency increase linked to land degradation, climate change, and health impacts (PM10 in India's Thar region)

concepts.name: Thar Desert Landforms: Indian Context and Aeolian Features
key_dimensions: Aeolian landforms of Thar: longitudinal/transverse dunes (barchans near Jaisalmer), interdune corridors, sandy plains (marusthali)
Role of Aravalli orientation in sand accumulation: Aravallis parallel to wind → no barrier → eastward sand migration into Gangetic plain
Palaeoclimatic evidence: fossil dunes (parabolic) in Punjab-Haryana indicating past arid extent; 'paleodunes' in UPSC physical geography
Policy dimension: Desert Development Programme, National Action Programme to Combat Desertification, and Central Arid Zone Research Institute (CAZRI), Jodhpur

concepts.name: Fossil/Relict Dunes and Palaeoclimatic Reconstruction
key_dimensions: Definition: stabilised, vegetated dunes formed under past arid conditions, now inactive — indicate former wind regimes and aridity
Examples: parabolic fossil dunes in Rajasthan, Kalahari linear dunes extending into humid Zimbabwe
Optically Stimulated Luminescence (OSL) dating as tool for establishing dune formation chronology
UPSC angle: fossil dunes as evidence for Last Glacial Maximum aridity expansion; link between aeolian and palaeoclimate questions
